scope.population: 2,480,092 rows of the trade-print panel with a finite markout and a finite non-negative notional, summed per wallet; the per-dollar distribution takes every wallet with no fill floor, and the headline net-toxic cut floors at 10 fills
scope.window: 10 days present in the input, day-of-month 4-13; the calendar dates of the window are declared by its producer, build_quickwin_markouts.py

declared_not_confirmed.note: settings.py declares these; this run did not state what it used, so they are the declaration and not a property of this artifact

_meta.headline: per_dollar_toxicity (notional-normalized markout)
_meta.cost_definition: sum(mo10/1e4 * notional) per wallet = maker loss (reported as DOLLAR COST, not toxicity)
_meta.framing_note: dollar cost is concentrated because trade size is concentrated; per-unit toxicity is only mildly concentrated and on average does not favour the taker -- see per_dollar_toxicity and the constant_toxicity_gini counterfactual
_meta.net_toxic_concentration_note: net-toxic concentration is reported at a HEADLINE min-fills cut (>= 10 fills); the unfiltered >= 1 cut is an inflated lower bound dominated by single-fill wallets. See per_dollar_toxicity.min_fills_sensitivity in each slice.
_meta.btc_vs_eth_split_caveat: the BTC-vs-ETH net-toxic-Gini gap is NOT a reliable finding: it is ~0.03 unfiltered and collapses to ~0.02 once tiny wallets are removed, and it has no standard error. Do not read a BTC/ETH toxicity-concentration difference from these numbers.
_meta.inference_note: headline net-toxic concentration carries a wallet-level bootstrap CI (per_dollar_toxicity.bootstrap_ci); all other figures are descriptive. The pdm>0 net-toxic selection is in-sample and biases the concentration upward (per_dollar_toxicity.selection_bias_note).
_meta.rank_floor_note: the headline net-toxic concentration floors wallets at 10 fills, and the >= 1 and >= 25 cuts sit beside it in min_fills_sensitivity; the per-dollar distribution over ALL wallets carries no floor at all

per_dollar_toxicity.measure: per-wallet mean markout (cost per unit notional, bps)

min_fills_1.label: INFLATED LOWER BOUND -- includes single-fill wallets whose one 10s markout self-selects on its own sign

bootstrap_ci.note: descriptive CI over wallet sampling only; does NOT correct the in-sample pdm>0 selection bias, which inflates the point estimate

per_dollar_toxicity.inference: bootstrap CI over wallets at the headline cut
per_dollar_toxicity.concentration_note: net_toxic_gini and toxic_top_*_share describe concentration AMONG net-toxic wallets only, at >= 10 fills; mean_bps (signed, over ALL wallets) is near-neutral/negative, so the average counterparty is not toxic
per_dollar_toxicity.min_fills_note: without a fills filter the net-toxic subset is dominated by tiny single-fill wallets carrying one noisy 10s markout; the >= 1 cut in min_fills_sensitivity is therefore an INFLATED LOWER BOUND and the headline uses >= 10 fills
per_dollar_toxicity.selection_bias_note: the net-toxic subset is selected by pdm > 0 using the SAME per-dollar markout that then measures its dispersion, so membership and dispersion share an in-sample selection that biases net_toxic_gini and the top-shares UPWARD; the bootstrap CI captures wallet-sampling noise only and does not remove this bias

dollar_cost.label: DOLLAR COST concentration (NOT toxicity) -- driven by trade size
dollar_cost.size_artifact_note: constant_toxicity_gini is the dollar-cost Gini with per-fill toxicity held at the global mean; its closeness to dollar_cost_gini shows how much of the dollar Gini is pure trade-size inequality

robustness.note: drop-top-k replaces the old single-whale check; notional_controlled compares each top-cost group's cost share to its notional share (ratio ~1 means cost concentration is trade size, not toxicity). Every top-k key names the criterion the k wallets are largest BY, which is gross dollar cost here
